children: Materials stocks remain closely tied to commodity cycles, industrial demand and input-cost trends, with earnings often influenced by fluctuations in metals prices, chemical demand and manufacturing activity.

The sector also encompasses businesses with very different exposure profiles, from specialty and commodity chemicals to mining and packaging, making company-level fundamentals particularly important as market conditions shift.

Against this backdrop, a quantitative screen identifies four materials-sector stocks that have maintained a Sell or Strong Sell Quant Rating for at least 60 consecutive days. The qualifying companies span specialty chemicals, diversified metals and mining, commodity chemicals, and metal, glass and plastic containers, covering several distinct areas of the materials value chain.
ASP Isotopes Inc.
leads the list, having maintained a Strong Sell Quant Rating for 107 consecutive days. Evolution Metals & Technologies Corp.
follows with 81 consecutive Strong Sell days, while United States Antimony Corporation
has held the rating for 77 days. PureCycle Technologies, Inc.
rounds out the list with 65 consecutive Strong Sell days.

All four companies have carried Strong Sell ratings for more than two months, placing them at the lower end of Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating scale. Their inclusion spans specialty materials, metals and mining, chemicals and plastics-related operations, highlighting the range of business models represented within the materials sector.

Seeking Alpha's Quant Ratings system grades stocks on their relative performance on key quantitative metrics. It hones in on stocks with the strongest combination of value, growth, profitability, EPS revisions and price momentum relative to their sector peers.
